title: Spacetime Emergence in the Memory of a Learning Agent
title_zh: 学习型智能体记忆中的时空涌现

paragraphs.en: We show that the causal structure of spacetime can emerge within the memory of a learning agent performing a quantum information task. We train a model-based reinforcement-learning agent to maximize the quantum mutual information between localized quantum probes interacting with a quantum field in Minkowski spacetime, without directly providing it with information regarding the spacetime metric or causal structure. In learning to accomplish this task, the reinforcement-learning agent constructs an internal predictive model whose planner develops the characteristic null structure of spacetime, allowing us to reconstruct the causal structure of the Minkowski metric with high accuracy. Within this task, spacetime geometry is obtained from an agent’s successful predictions and actions, providing a first step toward showing that spacetime concepts emerge from operational quantum experience.

paragraphs.en: General relativity is our most successful description of spacetime and has passed a remarkably broad range of experimental tests to date [ 64 ] , yet the geometry described by the theory — commonly represented by a Lorentzian metric tensor, which is an object encoding spacetime distances, angles, and causal relationships [ 61 , 14 ] — is never accessed directly in experiment but is instead inferred from the records left by physical systems interacting with matter and fields [ 14 , 3 ] . Whether through families of causal trajectories or the responses of localized detectors, every observation provides only finite operational information from which the underlying geometry must be reconstructed [ 57 , 14 , 47 , 23 , 36 , 52 , 44 , 19 ] . This operational viewpoint shifts the emphasis from geometry itself to the physical records encoding that geometry, motivating broader questions that lie at the heart of spacetime reconstruction: what kind of records are sufficient for an observer to recover the structure of the underlying spacetime and to what extent do they preserve the geometric information of the spacetime that generated them?
paragraphs.zh: 广义相对论是我们对时空最成功的描述，迄今已通过了范围极广的实验检验 [64]，然而该理论所描述的几何——通常由洛伦兹度规张量表示，它是编码时空距离、角度与因果关系的对象 [61, 14]——在实验中从未被直接接触，而是从与物质和场发生相互作用的物理系统留下的记录中推断出来 [14, 3]。 无论是通过因果轨迹族，还是通过局域探测器的响应，每一次观测都只提供有限的操作信息，而潜在的几何必须从这些信息中被重构出来 [57, 14, 47, 23, 36, 52, 44, 19]。 这一操作主义视角将关注重点从几何本身转移到编码该几何的物理记录上，由此引出处于时空重构核心的更广泛的问题：什么样的记录足以让观察者恢复潜在时空的结构？这些记录又在多大程度上保留了产生它们的时空的几何信息？

paragraphs.en: Multiple approaches have been developed to try and answer these questions, with quantum-information-based schemes being of particular interest with regards to what will be considered in the current work (introduced further down). For instance, Ref. [ 9 ] reconstructs spatial geometry from the entanglement structure of a Hilbert space factorization by using mutual information to define effective distances before fitting an emergent geometry. Ref. [ 26 ] advocates for replacing spacetime distance by correlation strength, treating abstract correlators as the primary structure from which spacetime and fields may arise as approximate descriptions. Additionally, Ref. [ 16 ] analyzes how relative distance can be associated with mutual information in entanglement-based emergent-spacetime scenarios while showing that simple entangled systems already contain ambiguities in such reconstructions.

paragraphs.en: Relativistic quantum information (RQI) arguably provides the most natural framework in which to address this question. In particular, Unruh–DeWitt (UDW) detectors [ 59 , 13 ] furnish a simple model of localized quantum systems interacting with quantum fields [ 15 , 18 ] while remaining sufficiently tractable that the resulting detector states can be analyzed using the tools of quantum information theory [ 35 , 41 , 38 ] . It is through these interactions that geometric and causal relationships as well as field correlations become encoded into finite-dimensional quantum states whose operational properties can be studied directly. UDW systems have consequently become one of the principal tools [ 10 ] for investigating how spacetime structure is reflected in quantum information, leading to a variety of protocols for reconstructing geometric quantities from detector data [ 39 , 44 , 52 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 相对论量子信息（RQI）可以说是解决这一问题最自然的框架。 特别是，Unruh–DeWitt（UDW）探测器 [ 59 , 13 ] 提供了一个描述局域量子系统与量子场相互作用的简单模型 [ 15 , 18 ] ，同时又足够易于处理，使得所得的探测器态可以用量子信息理论的工具进行分析 [ 35 , 41 , 38 ] 。 正是通过这些相互作用，几何关系、因果关系以及场的关联被编码到有限维量子态中，而这些量子态的操作性质可以被直接研究。 因此，UDW 系统已成为探究时空结构如何反映在量子信息中的主要工具之一 [ 10 ] ，并催生了多种从探测器数据重构几何量的协议 [ 39 , 44 , 52 ] 。

paragraphs.en: The perspective adopted here is somewhat different to the above mentioned works in that we ask whether a learning agent interacting only with operational quantum data sourced from quantum systems embedded in a spacetime (and with no a priori knowledge of spacetime), can itself acquire an internal representation that reflects the geometry of the spacetime generating those observations. The question is therefore whether successful interaction with a relativistic quantum environment naturally gives rise to representations from which that geometry can subsequently be extracted. Viewed in this way, a learning agent serves as a concrete operational observer whose internal memory is shaped by experience. More concretely, our setting considers model-based reinforcement-learning (RL) agents acting on an environment defined by the outcomes of a quantum information protocol performed in spacetime. RL converts the structure of that environment into a memory of actions that we can attempt to query to ascertain whether it contains a recoverable metric structure.
paragraphs.zh: 本文采用的视角与上述工作有所不同：我们探讨的是，一个仅与来自嵌入时空的量子系统所产生的操作性量子数据交互（且对时空没有任何先验知识）的学习智能体，能否自行获得一种反映产生这些观测的时空几何的内部表征。 因此，问题在于：与相对论性量子环境的成功交互，是否自然会催生出某种表征，使得之后可以从这些表征中提取出该几何。 以这种方式来看，学习智能体充当了一个具体的操作性观察者，其内部记忆由经验塑造。 更具体地说，我们的设定考虑的是基于模型的强化学习（RL）智能体，其作用于一个由在时空中执行的量子信息协议的结果所定义的环境。 强化学习将该环境的结构转化为一种动作记忆，我们可以尝试查询这一记忆，以确定其中是否包含可恢复的度量结构。

paragraphs.en: Our application of machine learning in pursuit of answering this question is a somewhat recent development with only a relatively small number of works employing the same strategy, and fewer still using RL. For example, the authors of Ref. [ 65 ] train a model on entanglement features so that the learned tensor-network geometry reproduces the entanglement structure of a quantum many-body state; the authors of Refs. [ 22 , 21 ] use deep learning in AdS/CFT-inspired settings to infer emergent bulk metrics from field-theoretic or lattice data, and more recently used interpretable neural architectures to reconstruct gravitational metrics from linear-response data [ 20 ] ; recent holographic reconstruction work uses entanglement-entropy data as input to a machine-learning inverse problem for the bulk metric [ 1 ] ; and in the RQI sphere, Ref. [ 17 ] uses deep learning to distinguish field states, detect field thermalization, and sense spacetime boundaries. Work on quantum-enhanced agents and causal machine learning in quantum settings comes closer still by treating agents as active participants whose actions and records mediate what can be learned about a quantum environment [ 54 ] . Our approach combines this active participant idea with RL in an RQI setting in a way that answers the original questions, but also distinguishes itself from these other works by drawing attention to the agentic aspect of learning new concepts from acting. In this respect, the problem is also related to work on intuitive physics and physical concept learning, where predictive models acquire internal representations of physical regularities from experience rather than having access to an explicit symbolic theory [ 48 ] .

paragraphs.en: To investigate these questions, we construct a detector-generated environment in which one Gaussian-smeared UDW detector remains fixed while a second is translated across a two-dimensional grid of spacetime smearing centres 𝗑 = ( x , t ) \mathsf{x}=(x,t) . Their interaction with a real massless scalar quantum field in ( 3 + 1 ) (3+1) -dimensional Minkowski spacetime, holding two spatial dimensions fixed, generates a transformed quantum mutual-information objective that provides the sole reward to a model-based RL agent with no initial conception of spacetime. The underlying spacetime structure is implicitly encoded in this reward and so the RL agent must learn a predictive representation of the environment — and thus the spacetime structure — through interaction with it. We then ask whether the memory supporting its successful behaviour retains enough of the structure underlying the operational quantum information for the spacetime geometry to be reconstructed from it. paragraphs.en: The UDW model bridges quantum information with relativity in a concrete way such that a learning task based on quantum information may be phrased in a spacetime setting. From the choice of a spacetime region to couple the detector to and a field state, one can determine the final finite-dimensional detector state whose correlations are then used to construct the reward landscape. The RL agent has access only to this resulting reward, while the spacetime geometry and field-theoretic quantities from which it is generated remain directly inaccessible. Each point in the environment therefore corresponds to a possible spacetime smearing centre for detector 2, with the value assigned to that point determined by the correlations induced through its interaction with the field.
paragraphs.zh: UDW 模型以一种具体的方式将量子信息与相对论联系起来，使得基于量子信息的学习任务可以在时空背景下表述。 通过选择一个将探测器与之耦合的时空区域以及一个场态，可以确定探测器最终的有限维状态，其关联随后被用于构建奖励景观。 强化学习中的智能体只能访问由此得到的奖励，而生成该奖励的时空几何和场论量仍然无法直接访问。 因此，环境中的每个点对应于探测器 2 的一个可能的时空涂抹中心，分配给该点的值由其与场的相互作用所诱导的关联决定。

paragraphs.en: UDW detectors were introduced as probes of quantum fields and observer-dependent particle content [ 59 , 13 , 58 ] . Their appeal in relativistic quantum information comes from the fact that a finite-dimensional quantum system can be coupled locally to a quantum field while keeping the operational output on the level of detector states. This has made the model remarkably useful for studying the transition probabilities, field noise, signalling, covariance, and the dependence of detector response on switching and localization [ 35 , 53 , 41 , 38 , 12 ] ; as well as providing a means for operationalizing spacetime properties into quantum information and computation resources for use in entanglement/contextuality harvesting [ 49 , 50 , 32 ] and relativistic quantum computing [ 37 , 8 , 40 , 2 , 30 ] . Work also shows how detector models capture fundamental features of the light-matter interaction [ 34 ] and how they extend to linearized-gravity settings [ 45 ] .
paragraphs.zh: UDW 探测器被引入作为量子场和依赖于观察者的粒子内容的探测工具 [ 59 , 13 , 58 ] 。 它们在相对论性量子信息中的吸引力在于：一个有限维量子系统可以与量子场局部耦合，同时将操作层面的输出保持在探测器态的层级上。 这使得该模型在研究跃迁概率、场噪声、信号传递、协变性以及探测器响应依赖于开关函数和局域化方面极为有用 [ 35 , 53 , 41 , 38 , 12 ] ；同时也提供了一种手段，可将时空性质操作化为用于纠缠/语境性收割的量子信息与计算资源 [ 49 , 50 , 32 ] ，以及用于相对论性量子计算 [ 37 , 8 , 40 , 2 , 30 ] 。 相关工作还表明，探测器模型如何捕捉光与物质相互作用的基本特征 [ 34 ] ，以及它们如何推广到线性化引力情形 [ 45 ] 。

paragraphs.en: The core idea of our paper is to allow an RL agent to move the second detector relative to the first, attempting to maximize the quantum mutual information between the two detectors after their interaction with the field. More precisely, we will describe t ¯ 2 \bar{t}_{2} and 𝒙 ¯ 2 \bar{\bm{x}}_{2} as values in a spacetime grid, constituting the RL agents’ environment. The RL agent then explores the environment by changing the spacetime placement of the second detector, receiving a reward function based on how well it is able to improve the quantum mutual information through local changes in t ¯ 2 \bar{t}_{2} and 𝒙 ¯ 2 \bar{\bm{x}}_{2} . This task updates the RL agent’s model of the environment and updates its memory at each step. We will discuss the task structure and the RL agent’s model in further detail in the following two sections.

paragraphs.en: As we are interested in an agentic perspective on learning spacetime structure, the problem is naturally formulated in terms of RL. paragraphs.en: There are two broad ways in which an RL agent can use experience to improve its decisions: model-free value-based methods and model-based methods. The model-free value-based methods, such as Q-learning [ 63 , 62 ] , directly learn the expected long-term return associated with taking an action in a state, which works quite well for small- to moderate-sized problems. For large state spaces, these value functions can be more efficiently represented by artificial neural networks, which provide flexible parameterized function approximators capable of generalizing between states rather than storing a separate value for every state-action pair [ 11 , 24 , 42 , 43 ] . Model-based methods on the other hand, have the RL agent instead learn an internal predictive model of the environment and use that model to evaluate possible actions before executing them [ 56 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 强化学习智能体利用经验改进其决策的方式大致有两种：无模型的价值方法和基于模型的方法。 无模型的价值方法，例如 Q-learning [ 63 , 62 ] ，直接学习在某个状态下执行某个动作所对应的期望长期回报，这对小到中等规模的问题效果相当好。 对于大型状态空间，这些价值函数可以更高效地用人工神经网络来表示，神经网络提供了灵活的参数化函数逼近器，能够在状态之间进行泛化，而不必为每个状态-动作对单独存储一个值 [ 11 , 24 , 42 , 43 ] 。 另一方面，基于模型的方法则让智能体学习环境的内部预测模型，并利用该模型在执行动作之前评估可能的动作 [ 56 ] 。

paragraphs.en: We adopt the model-based approach to model the RL agent’s memory and decision-making faculties, which in our case, consists of an encoder, decoder, transition model, reward model, and a planning rule that combines their predictions into a decision (see Fig. 1 for how these components fit together). We will refer to the collection of these learned internal models as the agent’s memory , since it is the orchestration of these learned models that retains the necessary behavioural information to act in the environment. This model-based approach is important for our purposes because the learned agent model provides explicit internal objects that can be interrogated after training, meaning that we can also examine whether the representations and predictions supporting its behaviour retain information about the spacetime structure that generated the reward landscape.

paragraphs.en: To learn the consequences of a broad range of actions, the RL agent must sometimes explore alternatives to the planner’s recommendations. The agent therefore follows the planner’s recommendation with probability 1 − ϵ 1-\epsilon and selects an action uniformly at random with probability ϵ \epsilon , where 0 ≤ ϵ ≤ 1 0\leq\epsilon\leq 1 . For a specified constant ϵ \epsilon , this is implemented by drawing a number u u uniformly from [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] : if u ≥ ϵ u\geq\epsilon , the agent follows the planner’s recommendation; otherwise, it samples an action uniformly from the available actions. This procedure is known as ϵ \epsilon -greedy exploration. paragraphs.en: In this section we introduce and describe the details of the learning task and parameter choices of the RL agent architecture. The question we are interested in addressing in this work is whether a learning agent performing a quantum information task that is embedded in spacetime — with no a priori notion of spacetime — can develop a representation of that spacetime within its memory after successfully completing the task. More concretely, given the predictive models and behaviour policy of a (model-based) RL agent tasked with maximizing a monotonic function of the quantum mutual information between two UDW qubit systems, both embedded in a spacetime, can we extract the causal or metric structure of the spacetime from them? The simplicity of the UDW model, combined with how it connects quantum information and spacetime geometry, makes it an ideal choice for setting up the problem environment. Note that from now on, we will hold two of the spatial dimensions of the ( 3 + 1 ) (3+1) dimensional spacetime fixed and consider a ( 1 + 1 ) (1+1) -dimensional slice.

paragraphs.en: As is standard practice when working with deep neural networks, the weights attached to the loss function terms are tuned so the learning scheme can be successful. The largest weight falls on the dynamics term because the planner needs a usable one-step latent model before its score surface can carry meaningful action information. The reward loss ties the latent transition to the environment reward, which is crucial for properly navigating the environment and completing the task, so it has a weight of 1. The latent transition loss terms also have relatively large weights because of the previously stated importance of the transition model. Finally, the decoder loss terms keep the latent representation tied to the observed detector grid, which is useful but not as important as the other terms, so they have small weights.

paragraphs.en: The training hyperparameters we used are as follows. The run uses N ep = 4000 N_{\rm ep}=4000 episodes with at most T max = 4000 T_{\max}=4000 environment steps per episode, which fixes the maximum number of detector placements the RL agent can sample before an episode terminates. Since the planner uses horizon H = 1 H=1 , its score contains only the predicted immediate reward, so γ = 0.97 \gamma=0.97 does not affect action selection and the reported episode return is likewise the undiscounted sum ∑ t r t + 1 \sum_{t}r_{t+1} of the shaped rewards. As we mentioned earlier, exploration is ϵ \epsilon -greedy with ϵ start = ϵ ⁡ ( 0 ) = 1.0 \epsilon_{\rm start}=\epsilon(0)=1.0 , ϵ final ∼ 0.1 \epsilon_{\rm final}\sim 0.1 (with a maximum number of steps n max = N ep ​ T max n_{\text{max}}=N_{\text{ep}}T_{\text{max}} ), and a step-based decay constant ϵ decay = 8.0 × 10 4 \epsilon_{\rm decay}=8.0\times 10^{4} . Episode starts are sampled uniformly during the first 35 % 35\% of training, from a 70 % 70\% uniform and 30 % 30\% edge-biased mixture during the next 35 % 35\% , and from a 40 % 40\% uniform and 60 % 60\% edge-biased mixture during the final phase. In each phase, the stated probabilities first select the corresponding region and the starting state is then sampled uniformly from that region, with edge starts drawn from a band of 25 25 cells near the grid boundary. This start schedule forces the planner to learn from longer moves across the finite grid rather than only from starts near the central high-information region, which assists in grid coverage and reinforcing far away states. The latent dimension is set to d z = 20 d_{z}=20 so the internal latent representation can be rich enough. paragraphs.en: The results from Section V provide a clear picture where an RL agent given a quantum information task embedded in a spacetime learns to accomplish that task while adhering to the geometry of the underlying spacetime. Through construction of a rich internal model of the environment that contains enough geometric and causal information, the agent is able to quantitatively reconstruct the Lorentzian metric of spacetime. Not only is the spacetime information implicitly hidden in the RL agent’s environment feedback—-in addition to the fact that the RL agent is initialized with no information about what spacetime is—-but the architecture of the RL agent also scrambles that information into an internal latent representation, disconnected with the exterior spacetime grid. This connects the present construction to work on intuitive physics , where agents can acquire internal representations supporting physical prediction without explicitly evaluating any equations of motion [ 4 , 27 , 48 ] . In particular, predictive models have been shown to acquire identifiable physical concepts from experience despite the absence of them in the explicit output of the prediction task [ 48 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 第V节的结果清晰地展示了：被赋予嵌入在时空中的量子信息任务的强化学习智能体，能够学会完成该任务，同时遵循底层时空的几何结构。 通过构建一个包含足够几何与因果信息的丰富内部环境模型，该智能体能够定量地重构时空的洛伦兹度规。 时空信息不仅隐式地隐藏在强化学习智能体的环境反馈中——而且该强化学习智能体在初始化时对时空是什么一无所知——此外，强化学习智能体的架构还将这些信息打乱成一种与外部时空网格脱节的内部潜在表示。 这将本文的构建与直觉物理方面的工作联系起来，在这类工作中，智能体能够在不显式求解任何运动方程的情况下，获得支持物理预测的内部表示 [ 4 , 27 , 48 ] 。 特别地，已有研究表明，尽管预测任务的显式输出中不含物理概念，预测模型仍能从经验中获得可识别的物理概念 [ 48 ] 。

paragraphs.en: This suggests an operational perspective on spacetime concept formation , where an RL agent does not need to possess an explicit symbolic representation of a Lorentzian manifold in order for spacetime structure to organize its behaviour. Instead, regularities in its interactions can become encoded as relations among internal states, predictions, and actions. In the present model the planner never explicitly evaluates g μ ​ ν ​ Δ ​ x μ ​ Δ ​ x ν = 0 g_{\mu\nu}\Delta x^{\mu}\Delta x^{\nu}=0 when choosing an action, yet the memory supporting those choices becomes sensitive to operational regularities from which this null condition can subsequently be recovered. In this restricted sense, the learned representation provides a primitive model of a spacetime concept as an action-relevant organization of experience that implicitly captures causal relations, analogous to the metric tensor. This is consistent with the view that memory goes beyond functioning as just an inert storage device, but plays a more active role as a resource for generating future behaviour [ 7 , 29 , 6 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 这表明对时空概念形成的一种操作性视角：强化学习智能体无需拥有洛伦兹流形的显式符号表示，时空结构也能组织其行为。 相反，其互动中的规律性可以被编码为内部状态、预测与行动之间的关系。 在本模型中，规划器在选择行动时从不显式地计算 g μ ​ ν ​ Δ ​ x μ ​ Δ ​ x ν = 0 g_{\mu\nu}\Delta x^{\mu}\Delta x^{\nu}=0，然而支持这些选择的记忆却对操作性规律变得敏感，由此可以随后恢复出这一零条件。 在这种受限的意义上，学到的表示提供了一个原始的时空概念模型，即作为一种与行动相关的经验组织，隐式地捕捉因果关系，类似于度量张量。 这与如下观点一致：记忆不仅仅是惰性的存储装置，而是作为生成未来行为的资源发挥更积极的作用 [ 7 , 29 , 6 ] 。

paragraphs.en: This point of view does highlight an important distinction however, which is that the RL agent does not carry the actual metric tensor object in its memory. As we saw earlier, it’s memory acquires a geometric flavour from learning, and the metric tensor is subsequently extracted using external tools supplied when studying it, such as lightcone masking and conformal gauge fixing. While using such geometrically informed post-processing procedures is unsatisfactory compared to the larger vision of explicitly emergent causal or metric structure in the RL agent’s memory, we view this work as merely a first step towards this setting. A stronger realization of this programme could of course make geometric inference itself part of the learned world model, for instance as a learned sub-network of the RL agent’s internal model.
paragraphs.zh: 然而这种观点确实突出了一个重要的区别，即强化学习智能体并不会在其记忆中携带实际的度规张量对象。 正如我们在前面看到的，它的记忆通过学习获得了几何的意味，而度规张量随后是在研究它时借助外部工具提取出来的，例如光锥掩蔽和共形规范固定。 与在强化学习智能体的记忆中显式涌现出因果或度规结构这一更大的愿景相比，使用这类基于几何的后处理程序并不令人满意，但我们把这项工作仅仅视为朝向这一目标的第一步。 这一计划的更强实现当然可以让几何推断本身成为学习到的世界模型的一部分，例如作为强化学习智能体内部模型的一个学习到的子网络。

Of course its recovery — particularly in the ( 1 + 1 ) (1+1) -dimensional case — is not in and of itself surprising, since the causal structure is known analytically and is already reflected in the known field correlations from which the detector data are generated. One should realize however, that the architecture and problem setup are agnostic to the underlying geometry of the data, so in the general setting they can still be employed to learn the structure even when it is not known in advance, meaning that the same strategy can be applied when detector generated quantum information is available but the spacetime from which it originates is not. More robust tests of the reconstruction under coordinate changes and different detector smearings should be undertaken as well before making this step. This would substantially strengthen the evidence that the learned relations represent spacetime structure as opposed to contingent properties of the chosen coordinates or probes.

paragraphs.en: The question of how far we can take this interpretation will require several extensions. First, quantum mutual information is not a pure measure of signalling as it contains both causally mediated and state-dependent correlations, including correlations at spacelike separation. Future agents should thus receive several complementary operational quantities that can tease these differences apart, such as signalling estimators or spin correlations, and more generally observables that are separately sensitive to commutator and anticommutator contributions. These may then allow for causal propagation and scale information to be distinguished and could provide the additional operational information required to reconstruct more than just the conformal structure. The setting should likewise be extended to ( 3 + 1 ) (3+1) -dimensional and curved spacetimes, where the local causal structure varies across the environment and cannot be identified with two globally straight lightcone branches like in Minkowski.
paragraphs.zh: 这一解释能走多远的问题将需要若干扩展。 首先，量子互信息并非纯粹的信号传递度量，因为它既包含因果中介的关联，也包含依赖态的关联，包括类空间隔处的关联。 因此，未来的智能体应获得若干互补的操作性量，以区分这些差异，例如信号传递估计器或自旋关联，以及更一般地对对易子和反对易子贡献分别敏感的可观测量。 这些量或可用于区分因果传播与尺度信息，并可提供额外的操作性信息，以重建的不只是共形结构。 情境同样应扩展到 ( 3 + 1 ) (3+1) 维以及弯曲时空，其中局域因果结构随环境变化，无法像在闵可夫斯基时空中那样用两条全局笔直的光锥分支来识别。

paragraphs.en: Finally, one can consider more challenging or practical quantum information tasks as the learning objective, since maximizing a scalar function of mutual information provides a nice transparent proof of principle, but a more compelling test would place the RL agent in a task for which learning spacetime structure is actually necessary for completing the task. Quantum communication or adaptive entanglement distribution through detector networks could be natural and interesting possibilities, which may also require the RL agent to utilize longer-horizon planning that would test how it progresses from implicitly exploiting causal regularities to constructing increasingly general representations of the spacetime in which it acts. The quantum information task studied here shows how the causal structure of Minkowski spacetime can emerge in the memory of an agent, opening the doors to the more ambitious question of whether agents can autonomously discover an explicit spacetime representation from operational experience alone.

paragraphs.en: Plot (a) displays the argmax action map and records how the planner partitions the grid into local action regions, clearly displaying the lightcone structure on the diagonals but also drawing attention to different local action domains. Plots (b) and (c) give the decoded coordinates which unambiguously show that the x x and t t coordinate organization is preserved by the encoder and decoder. Plot (d) gives the latent norm, which remains finite and spatially structured over the grid, and indicates that the latent state components are better shaped as we move closer to the goal state. Plots (e) and (f) display the action-conditioned dynamics error and the mean predicted latent step norm, both of which have the lightcone structure somewhat visible in them, with the first indicating that action-conditioned dynamics becomes slightly less reliable the further away from the goal that we move, and the second showing that the imagined latent displacement across the grid remains fairly controlled. Plots (g)—(i) show that the next-state reconstruction errors remain small away from the extreme boundary region. Finally, plots (j)—(l) compare three reward model projections: the mean over actions, the maximum over actions, and the reward assigned to the planner-selected action. Their common lightcone-shaped support is consistent with the reward range reported in Sec. V and with the planner-step reward shown in Fig. 5 . Thus, all plots are consistent with and support the narrative that the RL agent learned a useful representation of the spacetime to recover the Lorentzian quadratic form in Eq. ( 76 ).
